Instructions for the receiving Claude Code session

Read START_HERE_FOR_CLAUDE.md, the scope and permission specifications, and the page catalogue before editing. This folder is a developer handoff for a new academic web prototype. Do not infer production implementation from historical status labels or unrelated campus screens.

Use data/pages.json as the consolidated page catalogue. The two component page JSON files are authoring sources; tools/build_handoff.py merges them and builds the readable report. Edit those source files when updating page specifications. The UI prototype that you create is a separate deliverable: do not overwrite REPORT.html or historical reference HTML.

Treat W01-W60 as proposed web templates and O01-O03 as optional. Keep legacy S/P IDs as crosswalk references, not application routes. An optional assistant/award feature must not become a required menu item or a dependency of a core journey.

Preserve graded versus released, receipt versions, group membership at submission, explicit TA authority, personal calendar privacy, and source ownership. A role picker is a prototype aid, not authentication. Never reveal staff-only fields while rendering a student view. Show simulated saves/delivery/imports as samples. Do not claim localStorage is a secure academic record system.

Use plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript for the first reviewable design. Keep editable files under a separate prototype/ folder, plus an offline bundle if needed. Do not add React/Next, a paid UI service, a backend or a deployment merely to view the design. The frontend developer chooses their eventual stack. Use a deterministic scenario clock and fictional fixtures. Avoid network fonts, CDNs and real school/vendor logins in the offline artifact.

Honor browser/tool restrictions in the receiving environment. If local-file browsing is blocked, do not route around the restriction through localhost or another transport. Ask for permitted user-assisted visual inspection and distinguish that evidence from source checks. Do not claim that every browser/device has passed from one inspected environment.

Build in the stages in spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md. Finish complete journeys with controls that change the displayed sample record. Do not draw 60 disconnected cards and call the app complete. Where a function is deliberately not simulated, provide a clear explanatory state instead of fake success. For each stage, report pages, working transitions, scenario states, checks, limitations and next work in a developer-owned progress log.

Do not automatically commit, publish, message another person or upload the package. Do not copy the owner’s complete source folder to a third-party service. Do not overwrite reference resources. These instructions authorize frontend prototype design within the receiving user's request; production operations require their own scope.

Prompt to give your frontend developer's Claude Code

Copy the text below after extracting this ZIP and opening the extracted folder as the workspace.

> We are designing Whiteboard, an academic web app for students, instructors and teaching assistants. Read CLAUDE.md, README.md, spec/01_PRODUCT_AND_SCOPE.md, spec/02_NAVIGATION_AND_PERMISSIONS.md, spec/03_SHARED_UI_AND_STATES.md, spec/04_WORKFLOWS_AND_RECORDS.md, spec/05_BUILD_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md and spec/06_DECISIONS_AND_TRACEABILITY.md. Then inspect data/pages.json and data/fixtures.json. PAGE_CATALOGUE.md and REPORT.html contain the complete human-readable specifications. Resources are historical visual/source references, not scope expansion. > > Create the first HTML design prototype, with editable local HTML/CSS/JavaScript and an offline bundle, under a new prototype/ directory. Preserve the handoff and reference files. Use the Whiteboard visual identity, coherent course data, student/instructor/TA variants and all relevant recovery states. The frontend developer will refine the visual treatment afterward. Do not choose a production framework or build backend/auth/native services. > > Start by summarizing the academic scope, the proposed page inventory and the critical permission/state rules. Give a short stage plan, then implement Stage 1 from the build guide: the shared shell and the full assignment submission, grading and release journey. Continue through subsequent stages when the user asks, keeping a persistent progress checklist. Read every page specification needed by the current stage, and the connected pages before changing shared behavior. > > Use a visible, separate prototype role/scenario toolbar; never make it look like real product authentication. The actual app navigation must contain only authorized academic destinations. No campus events/clubs/bookings, direct messages or institution administration. Optional achievements and AI remain disabled unless explicitly selected. > > Make the normal and failure-path sample interactions work. Preserve immutable submission/release history and prevent TAs from releasing feedback or changing course policy. Support keyboard use, narrow web layouts, loading/empty/error/offline states and light/dark tokens. Do not treat an HTML phone frame as a native app. Validate in a permitted browser; if unavailable, report the limitation and request user-assisted inspection without bypassing a restriction. Never mark the full product implemented or accessible from source checks alone.

First output expected from Claude

An academic role shell and a navigable course-to-submission-to-feedback prototype, not a marketing landing page and not a redesigned report. The developer should be able to edit the visual CSS without changing course records, grade rules or navigation logic. Save implementation progress against W page IDs. Keep unbuilt pages visible only as clearly labeled prototype coverage entries outside the app shell; do not insert fake functional screens.
